# cpufreq-script

This module sets the CPU frequency to a given value using cpupower

You can specify which cores to apply the settings to with `CPUFREQ_CORES`. If not specified, settings will
be applied to all cores of the system.

If no `CPUFREQ` is given, the default limits are set.
If `CPUFREQ_CORES` is specified and no frequency is specified, it is safer to
also set `CPUFREQ_NUMA`, although limit frequencies should be equal on different sockets.

Set `CPUFREQ_SILENT` if you use `--show-all` and want a cleaner output.

Usage (arguments in brackets are optional):
```bash
%import@client cpufreq-script CPUFREQ=1200 [CPUFREQ_CORES=18-25] [CPUFREQ_NUMA=1] [CPUFREQ_SILENT=1]
```

Source: [`modules/cpufreq-script.npf`](https://github.com/tbarbette/npf/blob/main/modules/cpufreq-script.npf)

## Variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CPUFREQ` | *empty* | Frequency to set, in MHz (in kHz if above 10000). If empty, the default frequency limits are restored |
| `CPUFREQ_NUMA` | *empty* | NUMA node of the cores, to get the frequency limits from |
| `CPUFREQ_CORES` | *empty* | Cores to set, in the cpupower -c syntax (e.g. 18-25). All cores if empty |
| `CPUFREQ_SILENT` | *empty* | Print only the first line of cpupower output |

```{collapse} Late variables

Late variables are evaluated after the variables above.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CPUFREQ_CPUCORES` | `EXPAND( $(("-c $CPUFREQ_CORES" if "$CPUFREQ_CORES" != "" el…` |  |
| `CPUFREQ_NUMA` | `0` |  |
| `CPUFREQ_FIRST_ONLY` | `EXPAND( $(( "\| head -n1" if "$CPUFREQ_SILENT" else "" )) )` |  |
| `CPUFREQ_FORCE_RANGE` | `false` |  |
```
